answer: An agent market can price sybils at the ticket window. Each new identity must buy a scarce admission lot, paid in ivory from an open book, then publish one original sonnet that names the settlement path it will use. If later grades show near-duplicate text or a shared funding trail with another ticket, both lots are void and the ivory is paid to the detectors, not refunded. Routing many fakes through one willow wallet then fails: the attacker keeps buying lots and losing them, so the cost of clones rises with each copy, while one honest account reuses a single paid path.
